biography: Derek Parfit was a British moral philosopher whose work transformed debates about personal identity, reasons, and obligations to future people. His nonidentity cases show why an action can shape which people exist, making ordinary person-to-person comparisons difficult even when a policy leaves the future predictably worse. His population-ethics arguments also expose conflicts among plausible principles for comparing possible futures. PHIL 123 uses Parfit to show why counting future stakes is philosophically harder than multiplying a probability by a large number.

teaching.whyThisPerson: Parfit reveals how choices can affect who exists and why apparently simple future-benefit calculations produce deep moral conflicts.
